newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse opens lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse opens lower on profit-taking.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Thursday as investors took profits on the bourse's rally to record highs on the previous day.

Traders said investors were feeling cautious ahead of the U.S. consumer price index for April due at 1230 GMT. A 2.6 percent year-over-year increase is expected, or a rise of 0.2 percent in core inflation excluding food and energy prices.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.67, or 0.53 percent, at 2,759.96 at 0820 GMT. The CAC-40 May futures contract fell to 2,753.5 from 2,764 at Wednesday's close.
The broader SBF-120 index was down 8.19 points at 1,901.6.
Volume was 350 million francs in the first 10 minutes.
U.S. industrial production and capacity utilisation data are also due this afternoon but the market is focussing on the CPI for signs on future U.S. interest rate moves.

"If the CPI comes out better than expected, the market could test new highs today," one trader said. He sees resistance at the all time high of 2,781.87 points reached on Wednesday and major support at 2,726.

Fresh polls showing the conservatives likely to win a majority of seats in the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election had little impact on the bourse. Traders say the market is unlikely to show much reaction unless polls signal a sharp change in sentiment.
"The poll we're interested in is the one whose results we'll know on May 26," one trader said.
Shares in food group Danone rose against the trend, adding 0.11 percent to 918 francs, after chairman Franck Riboud's bullish remarks at the AGM on Wednesday.
